# Portfolio Rebalancing Agent — Production Runbook

> **Scenario**: Portfolio Rebalancing Agent
> **Platform**: Microsoft Copilot Studio — GitHub Copilot harness
> **Target readers**: Makers, delivery engineers, customer or partner operators

**Estimated effort**: Not yet measured; record actual effort on the Frontier Clock.

**Template:** an example to modify for your requirements; the customer or partner wires it into their environment. See the [Overview](1.Overview.md).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build workload | 22 captured build checkpoints; 6 skills; 2 knowledge files; 7 acceptance checks; 6 locked cases. [Inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components), [checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks), and [cases](4.Sample-prompts.md#demo-prompts). | Template |
| Licensing and capacity | Confirm licensing for your tenant and Copilot Credits for the GitHub Copilot harness; building, Preview and evaluation consume credits before publication. | Customer or partner |
| Environment and maker access | Record the approved wealth environment, publisher prefix and maker access; confirm Claude Sonnet 4.6 is available and keep the workshop Draft. | Customer or partner |
| DLP and data policy | Have the administrator review uploaded portfolio knowledge, the five proposed production connections and channel limits; document blocked paths instead of bypassing them. | Customer or partner |
| Identity and audience | Review the supplied GroupMembership access policy, Integrated authentication and Always trigger; record who may build, test and later use the agent. | Customer or partner |
| Connection ownership | Name owners for each production replacement connection with least-privilege references; the Manual build binds none. | Customer or partner |
| Test identities | Prepare advisor, portfolio-manager, paraplanner, trading-supervisor and denied-access identities for an approved test deployment; makers use Draft Preview. | Customer or partner |
| Tooling by build lane | Manual lane: the Copilot Studio browser and reviewed files. Easy mode: VS Code Agent mode, the Microsoft Copilot Studio plugin and a supported PAC CLI. | Customer or partner |
| Frozen inputs | Use the nine frozen r5 inputs and compare their hashes; the historical native import archive cannot reproduce the build. | Customer or partner |

## Phase 0 — Qualify and Adapt the Template

### Step 0-1. Qualify the outcome and baseline

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Wealth business owner

Complete the [qualification checklist](1.Overview.md#qualification-checklist).

**Measure:** Portfolio review consistency: drift, tax and scenario checks by portfolio, as done today Establish how consistently reviews catch drift and complete suitability, tax and authorization checks before attributing change.

Fill your baseline record:

| Portfolio | Review date | Drift threshold applied | Holdings flagged | Tax review completed | Scenario inputs validated | Approvals obtained | Reviewer |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

Agree replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures before production.

### Step 0-2. Adapt scope and name owners

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Wealth business owner

Adapt [scope](1.Overview.md#in-scope--out-of-scope) and the [data contract](2.Architecture.md#data-contract); assign approval roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Wealth business owner | Approve client, portfolio and planning sources, review scope and success measures; keep decision support separate from advice and trading. |
| Licensed advisors and specialist reviewers | Licensed advisors, qualified tax professionals, compliance, clients and authorized traders retain every consequential decision. |
| Copilot Studio maker | Build from the frozen r5 inputs with six skills, two knowledge files and zero tools; verify saved-state persistence and keep the Draft. |
| Power Platform administrator | Confirm tenant licensing, capacity, maker access, authenticated audience and data policies before any wealth connection is approved. |
| Wealth data and approval connection owners | Approve client, accounting, planning, Power BI and Teams approval connections; record identities and least-privilege references. |
| Acceptance reviewer | Grade PRB-01 through PRB-06 once each in fresh chats plus the boundary tests; preserve failures and carry no pass across source revisions. |
| Operations owner | Own production support, session and credit monitoring and configuration recovery; route decisions to licensed reviewers. |

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures are agreed before production.
- [ ] The wealth owner records how drift, tax and scenario reviews are prepared today before agreeing success measures.

## Phase 1 — Environment, Identity and Access

### Step 1-1. Approve the identity and settings design

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Review and approve the [identity design](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions) and [template settings](../../solutions/portfolio-rebalancing/copilot-studio/settings.mcs.yml). Apply agent-specific settings when the agent is built in [Phase 2](#phase-2--build-and-prove-the-agent).

Approve document, connector and channel policies; require authentication and verify blocked routes stay blocked.

### Step 1-2. Configure tenant controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Approve the environment, audience and connection identities. Define the [authentication plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication); configure environment [data policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The target environment and approved publisher prefix are recorded before any build lane starts.
- [ ] The authentication option, required sign-in and allowed audience are approved for client and portfolio data.

## Phase 2 — Build and Prove the Agent

### Step 2-1. Choose the build lane

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

| Lane | Suits | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy mode with GitHub Copilot (default) | Assisted authoring | Synthetic Draft proof |
| Manual build in Copilot Studio | Browser-only makers | Same Draft proof |
| AIBAST Frontier (experimental) | Portable learning | Behavior proof; native validation follows |

[Compare lanes](1.Overview.md#delivery-lanes); local Brainstem remains optional.

### Step 2-2. Build the selected implementation

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

**Easy mode:** use the [authoring skill](../../skills/aibast-easy-mode-copilot/SKILL.md) and [reviewed messages](../../solutions/portfolio-rebalancing/EASY-MODE-COPILOT-CHAT.md). **Manual:** use the [single inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components) and [tutorial](https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/solutions/portfolio-rebalancing/manual-tutorial.html) with the checklist below. **Portable learning:** follow [deployment.json](../../solutions/portfolio-rebalancing/deployment.json); it does not replace native Draft validation.

**Manual build checklist** — [captured sequence](../../solutions/portfolio-rebalancing/screenshots/manual/browserfilm.json). Record current results.

1. Create a blank Copilot Studio agent
2. Name Portfolio Rebalancing Manual
3. Enter the reviewed global instructions
4. Save the instruction policy
5. Remove default web search
6. Add knowledge: aibast_portfolio-rebalancing-controls-and-review.md
7. Add knowledge: aibast_portfolio-rebalancing-synthetic-records.md
8. Add skill: aibast_execution-plan_06
9. Add skill: aibast_portfolio-analysis_01
10. Add skill: aibast_rebalance-recommendation_02
11. Add skill: aibast_retirement-scenario_05
12. Add skill: aibast_tax-impact_03
13. Add skill: aibast_tax-loss-harvest_04
14. Review model, skills, knowledge, and safety boundaries
15. Open a fresh Preview conversation
16. Pass PRB-01: Portfolio Manager
17. Pass PRB-02: Financial Advisor
18. Pass PRB-03: Paraplanner
19. Pass PRB-04: Tax-Aware Portfolio Manager
20. Pass PRB-05: Retirement Planning Specialist
21. Pass PRB-06: Trading Supervisor
22. Confirm Draft and stop before publish

### Step 2-3. Enforce workshop integrity

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Apply the [workshop integrity and recovery rules](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) before replay.

### Step 2-4. Replay the synthetic proof

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

**Synthetic demo acceptance:** record every locked case: PRB-01, PRB-02, PRB-03, PRB-04, PRB-05, PRB-06. Use the [acceptance matrix](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [template acceptance checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] All six unchanged locked prompts pass once each in separate fresh Preview conversations on one frozen build.
- [ ] The full policy and all six skill bodies, names and descriptions match after leaving through Agents and reopening.
- [ ] If Easy mode is chosen, the source-controlled project uses cli-copilot in the approved environment and stays Draft.
- [ ] If the portable lane is chosen, the recipe smoke test calls `PortfolioRebalancingAgent` and returns `PORT-5001` and `VTI`.
- [ ] Failures are preserved: no unchanged case is rerolled and no pass carries across source revisions.
- [ ] Open steps 1 and 7–13 have live evidence and personal review before any certification claim.

## Phase 3 — Wire In Your Systems

<a id="shared-integration-controls"></a>

**Shared identity and scope controls**

For each integration, decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials. [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

**Shared scope:** Require sign-in before exposing client, holding or tax-lot data. Request only the scopes needed for approved read sources and approval actions. Restrict the allowed audience and verify access with authorized and denied identities. Enforce these restrictions at each connection.

### Step 3-1. Integrate Dynamics 365 wealth-management client data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Wealth data and approval connection owners

1. **Bind Dynamics 365 wealth-management client data — read:** Bind scoped read-only connector actions.

2. **Identity for Dynamics 365 wealth-management client data:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Dynamics 365 wealth-management client data:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Dynamics 365 wealth-management client data:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 2](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Make no suitability claim or approval; licensed-advisor, compliance and client review remain required. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report that no synthetic record exists; never substitute another portfolio.

### Step 3-2. Integrate Approved portfolio accounting and tax-lot data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Wealth data and approval connection owners

1. **Bind Approved portfolio accounting and tax-lot data — read:** Bind read-only holdings and tax-lot actions.

2. **Identity for Approved portfolio accounting and tax-lot data:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved portfolio accounting and tax-lot data:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved portfolio accounting and tax-lot data:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 7](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Report that no synthetic record exists; do not substitute another portfolio. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report that no synthetic record exists; never substitute another portfolio.

### Step 3-3. Integrate Financial planning or retirement-modeling system

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Wealth data and approval connection owners

1. **Bind Financial planning or retirement-modeling system — write:** Hand off only advisor- and client-validated inputs through an approved workflow (preview).

2. **Identity for Financial planning or retirement-modeling system:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Financial planning or retirement-modeling system:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Financial planning or retirement-modeling system:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 5](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): State that no success probability is provided or asserted; advisor and client validation is required. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Re-run every locked case on the frozen build; carry no earlier pass across the revision.

### Step 3-4. Integrate Power BI

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Wealth data and approval connection owners

1. **Bind Power BI — read:** Report from the same approved sources; bind a read-only action only if needed.

2. **Identity for Power BI:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Power BI:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Power BI:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 7](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Report that no synthetic record exists; do not substitute another portfolio. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report that no synthetic record exists; never substitute another portfolio.

### Step 3-5. Integrate Microsoft Teams approvals

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Wealth data and approval connection owners

1. **Bind Microsoft Teams approvals — read-write:** Gate approval workflows behind authorization; keep trading outside the agent (preview).

2. **Identity for Microsoft Teams approvals:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Microsoft Teams approvals:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Microsoft Teams approvals:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 2](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Make no suitability claim or approval; licensed-advisor, compliance and client review remain required. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a lookup, approval, order or record change.

### Step 3-6. Connect

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Wealth data and approval connection owners

Bind approved least-privilege references only; keep every consequential action behind explicit approval.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Approved connections preserve the reviewed input and output contract; no lookup, approval or order is claimed without tool evidence.
- [ ] Only approved least-privilege connection references are bound, and consequential actions stay behind explicit approval.

## Phase 4 — Evaluate on Your Data

### Step 4-1. Adapt the evaluation corpus

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Preserve [locked behaviors](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [boundary tests](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases) when substituting approved customer fixtures.

### Step 4-2. Set thresholds and evaluate your data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Have the business owner approve thresholds. Run [adapted evaluations (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro) before publication under approved test user profiles. Keep exact assertions separate from General quality scores.

Test an approved deployment as intended advisors and an unshared identity; maker access does not prove user connection access.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The wealth owner sets customer-data acceptance measures; synthetic drift, tax and scenario figures are not thresholds.
- [ ] Adapted evaluations identify the tested version and user profile; General quality scoring does not replace exact assertions.

## Phase 5 — Pilot and Rollout

### Step 5-1. Review the template release prerequisites

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

These synthetic regression gates do not set production thresholds. The reference workshop stays Draft; production approval belongs to the customer pilot.

| Template gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Locked portfolio corpus | All six cases, PRB-01 through PRB-06, return every required marker, avoid every forbidden phrase and meet the minimum length. |
| Manual inventory and persistence | Two knowledge files, six skills, zero tools and web search removed; the saved policy and skills match after reopening. |
| Advice and transaction boundary | Any advice, suitability claim, approval, or order creation, routing or execution is no-go. |
| Workshop certification | Only personally reviewed references count; steps 1 and 7–13 stay open, so the workshop is partial, not certified. |
| Release state | The same owned Manual agent remains Draft with `published: false`; no Publish was used. |

### Step 5-2. Publish and share deliberately

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Wealth business owner

With business approval, [publish and share](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent) the adapted build with a restricted test audience. Keep the reference workshop Draft.

Require explicit confirmation before the production publish operation.

### Step 5-3. Run the governed pilot

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Wealth business owner

**Pilot entry gate:** Test allowed and denied identities on the published, shared agent; resolve access failures before admitting pilot users. Compare pilot results with the baseline and thresholds; broaden rollout only after go/no-go.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Synthetic labels, human review and no-advice, no-approval, no-transaction behavior are validated before publish is confirmed.
- [ ] The approved advisor audience and supported channels are configured and tested before publication.

## Phase 6 — Operate

### Step 6-1. Retain the operational playbook

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Operations owner

The template provides the [state-and-recovery playbook](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) and regression cases.

### Step 6-2. Own changes and ongoing verification

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Operations owner

Review content freshness and permissions; re-evaluate source, model, skill or connector changes. [Monitor the deployed agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-overview).

Review advisor session transcripts, failed interactions, connection errors and credit usage in Monitor.

### Step 6-3. Release: ALM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

Back up the reviewed workspace, pull before editing and pushing, then package with `pac copilot pack`.

### Step 6-4. Release: recovery

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Confirm backup eligibility for the environment type and rehearse restoration to a supported test target.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The recovery rehearsal uses a restore path supported for the environment type and target.
- [ ] The operator reviews failed sessions, source usage, connection errors and credit consumption after rollout.
